limitations: Targeted stages 458–467 and regression stages 170–467 passed; the full project suite was not run.
External payment provider and sandbox were not tested; real-money processing remains NO-GO.
ISO-8601 timestamp checks and SQLite validation are local structural checks, not cryptographic authenticity guarantees.
Backup/restore tests do not establish disaster-recovery RPO/RTO, off-host durability, filesystem crash consistency, or distributed exactly-once execution.
focus: ISO-8601 timezone-aware audit timestamps, contradiction detection, read-only backup validation, corrupt SQLite rejection, temporary-file cleanup, no-overwrite behavior, repeated recovery, and end-to-end audit recovery.
safety_boundary: Backup validation checks local SQLite integrity, schema version, required columns, execution-index definition, record decoding, and reconciliation audit timestamp/consistency; it does not prove authenticity or off-host durability.
Backup publication uses a same-directory temporary file and atomic hard-link creation to avoid overwriting an existing destination; filesystem-specific behavior still requires deployment testing.
Restore checks cover exercised local SQLite scenarios only and do not establish disaster-recovery RPO/RTO.
Local SQLite tests do not establish distributed exactly-once execution.
Real-money payment processing remains prohibited until provider and sandbox integration are independently verified.
